--- title: "Where the World Burns: Wildfires on Every Continent Since 2002" description: "Wildfires on every continent in satellite data: how much of Africa, Europe and the rest of the world burns each year, whether the world burns more than it used to, what burns, when each continent burns, and the worst years." author: "" date: "27 November 2026" --- ## What is this? Every summer the fires of California, Canada, Australia or Greece make the news. They are a small part of the land that burns in the world: most of it burns in Africa, every year, in dry seasons that seldom make the news at all. This story compares the continents and asks five questions: 1. **Where in the world does land burn?** 2. **Is the world burning more than it used to?** 3. **What burns: forest, savanna, grassland or fields?** 4. **When does each continent burn?** 5. **Which were the worst years?** [Greece Burning](ILLUSTRATION_GREEK_WILDFIRES.html) looks at one country close up; this page looks at the whole world. The data come from the **Global Wildfire Information System** (GWIS), a joint initiative of the Group on Earth Observations and the EU's Copernicus programme, funded mainly by the European Commission ([GWIS](https://gwis.jrc.ec.europa.eu/)). Our World in Data adds up its figures by continent ([Wildfires](https://ourworldindata.org/wildfires)), and they are downloaded from there when the page is rendered: - **The land burnt each year since 2002 in every country**, mapped by NASA's MODIS sensors on the Terra and Aqua satellites, which find land that has just burnt in their images (the product MCD64A1, [Giglio et al. 2018](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.rse.2018.08.005)), with the kind of land that burnt: forest, savanna, shrubland and grassland, cropland or other land ([GWIS country profiles](https://gwis.jrc.ec.europa.eu/apps/country.profile/downloads)). - **The land burnt each week since 2012**, from MODIS and the finer VIIRS sensors, and the **carbon dioxide** that the fires released each year since 2003 ([GWIS seasonal trends](https://gwis.jrc.ec.europa.eu/apps/gwis.statistics/seasonaltrend)). - **The land area of each country**, from the World Bank ([land area](https://ourworldindata.org/grapher/land-area-km)), and the continent it is in ([continents](https://ourworldindata.org/grapher/continents-according-to-our-world-in-data)). A **hectare** is a square of 100 metres by 100, so a million hectares are 10,000 square kilometres. **The satellites count every fire.** They map the land that burnt, whatever started the fire: a wildfire, a farmer burning the stubble of a field, or a fire set on purpose to clear dry grass. And they miss some: small fires, and fires hidden by cloud or by the trees above them ([Our World in Data](https://ourworldindata.org/grapher/annual-area-burnt-by-wildfires-gwis)). --- ## Packages ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # install.packages("plotly") library(plotly) ``` ::: ## The data ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # a chart of Our World in Data as a table: one row for each country or region and each year (or # week) owid<-function(chart) { result<-read.csv(paste0("https://ourworldindata.org/grapher/",chart, ".csv?v=1&csvType=full&useColumnShortNames=true")) return(result) } # the land burnt each year, in hectares, by the kind of land (MODIS) cover<-owid("annual-burned-area-by-landcover") # the land burnt each week, in hectares (MODIS and VIIRS); the weeks are written as "2012-W01" weekly<-owid("weekly-area-burnt-by-wildfires") # the carbon dioxide that the fires released each year, in tonnes (MODIS and VIIRS) co2<-owid("annual-carbon-dioxide-emissions") # the land area of each country, in square kilometres (World Bank), and the continent it is in land<-owid("land-area-km") continents<-owid("continents-according-to-our-world-in-data") ``` ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # the kinds of land: the columns of the data and their names on this page covers<-c(forest="Forest",savannas="Savanna",shrublands_grasslands="Shrubland and grassland", croplands="Cropland",other="Other land") cover$all<-rowSums(cover[names(covers)]) first_year<-min(cover$year) last_year<-max(cover$year) first_five<-first_year:(first_year+4) last_five<-(last_year-4):last_year # the continents of Our World in Data, which counts all of Russia in Europe, with Russia on its own by_group<-function(x,time="year") { values<-setdiff(names(x),c("entity","code",time)) europe<-x[x$entity=="Europe",] russia<-x[x$entity=="Russia",] russia<-russia[match(europe[[time]],russia[[time]]),] rest<-europe rest[values]<-europe[values]-russia[values] rest$entity<-"Europe without Russia" others<-c("Africa","Asia","North America","Oceania","South America","Russia") y<-rbind(x[x$entity%in%others,],rest) names(y)[names(y)=="entity"]<-"group" return(y) } yearly<-by_group(cover) world<-cover[cover$entity=="World",] # the groups, from the one that burns the most land to the one that burns the least groups<-names(sort(tapply(yearly$all,yearly$group,mean),decreasing=TRUE)) # the groups and the world in one table, the world first with_world<-rbind(yearly[,c("group","year","all",names(covers))], data.frame(group="World",world[,c("year","all",names(covers))])) with_world$group<-factor(with_world$group,levels=c("World",groups)) # the countries: rows with a country code that Our World in Data puts on a continent (its regions, # such as "Europe (excl. Russia)", have no code or one that starts with OWID_, like Kosovo's) country_codes<-continents$code[nzchar(continents$code)] group_of<-function(code) { continent<-continents$owid_region[match(code,continents$code)] result<-ifelse(code=="RUS","Russia",ifelse(continent=="Europe","Europe without Russia",continent)) return(result) } # each country: the land burnt in an average year, its land area (the latest year that the World # Bank has) and its group countries<-aggregate(cbind(burnt=all,crops=croplands)~code+entity, data=cover[cover$code%in%country_codes,],FUN=mean) countries<-countries[order(countries$code,method="radix"),] rownames(countries)<-NULL land_now<-land[land$code%in%country_codes&!is.na(land$ag_lnd_totl_k2),] land_now<-land_now[order(land_now$code,-land_now$year),] land_now<-land_now[!duplicated(land_now$code),] countries$km2<-land_now$ag_lnd_totl_k2[match(countries$code,land_now$code)] countries$group<-group_of(countries$code) # a hectare is 1% of a square kilometre, so hectares per square kilometre are a percentage countries$share<-countries$burnt/countries$km2 ``` ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} red<-"#d62728" gray<-"#bdbdbd" dark_gray<-"#6b6b6b" # also the colour of the notes # the kinds of land, in the order of the stacked bars, whose neighbours were checked for colour # blindness; the other land, a sliver, is grey cover_colors<-c(forest="#008300",savannas="#eda100",shrublands_grasslands="#1baf7a", croplands="#eb6834",other="#d9d9d9") # one hue, from light to dark, for amounts: the map and the calendar oranges<-c("#feedde","#fdd0a2","#fdae6b","#fd8d3c","#f16913","#d94801","#8c2d04") # the source of a plotly chart, as a note under it, and the common layout chart<-function(p,title,source,y_title="",y_axis=list(),x_axis=list(),annotations=list(), margin=list(t=70,b=90),note_y=-0.16,...) { note<-list(text=paste("Source:",source),xref="paper",yref="paper",x=0,y=note_y,xanchor="left", yanchor="top",showarrow=FALSE,font=list(size=11,color=dark_gray)) result<-layout(p,title=list(text=title,x=0.02,xanchor="left",y=0.97,yanchor="top"), yaxis=c(list(title=y_title),y_axis),xaxis=c(list(title=""),x_axis),margin=margin, annotations=c(annotations,list(note)),...) %>% config(displaylogo=FALSE) return(result) } legend_top<-list(orientation="h",x=0,y=1.02,yanchor="bottom") # a colour scale of steps for classes numbered 1, 2, ... (with zmin = 0.5): one colour for each # class color_steps<-function(colors) { n<-length(colors) result<-do.call(c, lapply(seq_len(n),function(i) list(list((i-1)/n,colors[i]),list(i/n,colors[i])))) return(result) } # numbers in the text number<-function(x) { result<-format(round(x),big.mark=",",scientific=FALSE,trim=TRUE) return(result) } percent<-function(x,digits=0) { result<-paste0(format(round(x,digits),nsmall=digits,trim=TRUE),"%") return(result) } one<-function(x) { result<-format(round(x,1),nsmall=1,trim=TRUE) return(result) } two<-function(x) { result<-format(round(x,2),nsmall=2,trim=TRUE) return(result) } # millions (of hectares or tonnes): whole numbers from 10 million, one decimal below million<-function(x) { result<-ifelse(abs(x)>=1e7,number(x/1e6),one(x/1e6)) return(result) } # a change in per cent, with its sign change_text<-function(x) { result<-paste0(ifelse(x>=0,"+","−"),round(abs(x)),"%") return(result) } and_list<-function(x) { if(length(x)<2) { return(paste(x)) } result<-paste(paste(head(x,-1),collapse=", "),"and",tail(x,1)) return(result) } # country names that take "the" in a sentence with_the<-function(x) { with_article<-c("Central African Republic","Democratic Republic of Congo","United States", "Gambia") result<-ifelse(x%in%with_article,paste("the",x),x) return(result) } # a rank test of a trend over the years: the chance, in 100, of a pattern as strong as this one # without a trend chance<-function(x,years) { p<-cor.test(years,x,method="kendall",exact=FALSE)$p.value result<-if(p<0.01) "less than 1" else as.character(round(100*p)) return(result) } ``` ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # the weekly figures: the year, and the week (the 53rd week of the years that have one counts as the # 52nd, so that every year has the same weeks) week_parts<-function(x) { x$year<-as.integer(substr(x$week,1,4)) x$w<-pmin(as.integer(substr(x$week,7,8)),52) return(x) } weekly<-week_parts(weekly) # the month of a week: that of its middle day, near enough month_of<-function(w) { result<-as.integer(format(as.Date("2001-01-01")+7*(w-1)+3,"%m")) return(result) } first_week_year<-min(weekly$year) last_season<-2024 # the last year of the weekly figures and the carbon dioxide used here (below) # for the world, the weekly figures of each year added up, against the yearly MODIS figures weekly_world<-weekly[weekly$entity=="World",] agree<-aggregate(cbind(weekly=area_ha)~year,data=weekly_world,FUN=sum) agree<-merge(agree,world[,c("year","all")],by="year") agree$ratio<-100*agree$weekly/agree$all before<-agree[agree$year<=last_season,] # April to September: weeks 14 to 39 mid_year<-aggregate(cbind(area=area_ha)~year,data=weekly_world[weekly_world$w%in%14:39,],FUN=sum) mid_before<-mid_year$area[mid_year$year<=last_season] modis_before<-world$all[world$year%in%before$year] ``` ::: **The continents are those of Our World in Data, with Russia on its own.** Our World in Data counts all of Russia in Europe. But most of Russia is in Asia, and Russia burns 5 times as much land as the rest of Europe put together: as part of Europe, it would hide everything else. **The weekly figures, and the carbon dioxide, stop at 2024.** From 2012 to 2024, the weekly figures of a year added up to between 93% and 120% of the yearly MODIS figure for the world; in 2025, to 81%. From April to September 2025 they add up to 141 million hectares, against 200 to 261 in the same months of the years before, while the yearly MODIS figure for 2025, 333 million hectares, is within the range of the years before it (331 to 454). The weekly figures may have changed the way they are made; until the two series agree again, this page uses them, and the carbon dioxide that comes with them, only up to 2024. --- ## 1. Where in the world does land burn? ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} mean_by_group<-aggregate(cbind(burnt=all)~group,data=yearly,FUN=mean) mean_by_group$world_share<-100*mean_by_group$burnt/mean(world$all) # the share of its land, from the countries whose land area the World Bank has with_land<-countries[!is.na(countries$km2),] group_land<-aggregate(cbind(burnt,km2)~group,data=with_land,FUN=sum) at<-match(mean_by_group$group,group_land$group) mean_by_group$land_share<-group_land$burnt[at]/group_land$km2[at] in_group<-function(g,column) { result<-mean_by_group[[column]][mean_by_group$group==g] return(result) } world_burnt<-mean(world$all) world_land_share<-sum(with_land$burnt)/sum(with_land$km2) eu<-land[land$entity=="European Union (27)",] eu_hectares<-100*eu$ag_lnd_totl_k2[which.max(eu$year)] in_country<-function(name,column) { result<-countries[[column]][countries$entity==name] return(result) } most_burnt<-head(with_land[order(-with_land$share),],4) n_years<-last_year-first_year+1 europe_rest<-countries[countries$group=="Europe without Russia",] ukraine_part<-100*in_country("Ukraine","burnt")/sum(europe_rest$burnt) ``` ::: **Africa: two thirds of all the land that burns.** From 2002 to 2025, fires burnt 397 million hectares of the world's land in an average year, about as much as all the land of the European Union (399 million hectares), and 3.1% of the land of the world. 67% of it was in Africa: 267 million hectares a year, as much as 9% of the continent. Oceania, almost all of it Australia, had 11% of the world's burnt land, South America 8% and Asia 7%. Russia had 3.1%, North America 2.2% and the rest of Europe 0.6%. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} bars<-mean_by_group[order(mean_by_group$burnt),] # the largest at the top bars$group<-factor(bars$group,levels=bars$group) bar_colors<-ifelse(bars$group=="Africa",red,gray) left<-plot_ly(bars,x=~burnt/1e6,y=~group,type="bar",orientation="h",marker=list(color=bar_colors), text=~paste0(million(burnt)," (",percent(world_share),")"),textposition="outside", cliponaxis=FALSE, hovertemplate="%{y}: %{x:.1f} million hectares a year", showlegend=FALSE) right<-plot_ly(bars,x=~land_share,y=~group,type="bar",orientation="h",marker=list(color=bar_colors), text=~percent(land_share,1),textposition="outside",cliponaxis=FALSE, hovertemplate="%{y}: %{x:.1f}% of its land a year",showlegend=FALSE) hidden_axis<-list(title="",showticklabels=FALSE,showgrid=FALSE,zeroline=FALSE) panel_title<-function(text,axis) { result<-list(text=text,xref=paste(axis,"domain"),yref="paper",x=0,y=1,xanchor="left", yanchor="bottom",showarrow=FALSE,font=list(size=13)) return(result) } # the left panel wider: its labels are longer subplot(left,right,shareY=TRUE,margin=0.04,widths=c(0.6,0.4)) %>% chart(paste0("Land burnt in an average year, ",first_year,"–",last_year), "GWIS (MODIS), via Our World in Data; land areas: World Bank.", x_axis=c(hidden_axis,list(range=c(0,1.75*max(bars$burnt)/1e6))), xaxis2=c(hidden_axis,list(range=c(0,1.45*max(bars$land_share)))), annotations=list(panel_title("Million hectares (and share of the world)","x"), panel_title("Share of its own land","x2")), margin=list(l=150,t=90,b=50,r=10),note_y=-0.06) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: **Some countries burn a large part of their land every year.** In South Sudan, the land burnt in an average year adds up to 47% of the country: over the 24 years, 11 times the whole country, so the same land burns again and again. Zambia (31%), the Central African Republic (30%) and Angola (30%) come next, all in the belts of grassland and scattered trees north and south of Africa's rainforest. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} on_map<-countries[!is.na(countries$share),] classes<-c(0,0.1,0.5,1,5,10,20,Inf) class_names<-c("Under 0.1%","0.1–0.5%","0.5–1%","1–5%","5–10%","10–20%","20% or more") on_map$class<-as.integer(cut(on_map$share,classes,right=FALSE)) plot_ly(on_map,type="choropleth",locations=~code,z=~class,zmin=0.5,zmax=7.5, colorscale=color_steps(oranges),marker=list(line=list(color="white",width=0.3)), text=~paste0(entity,": ",ifelse(share<1,two(share),one(share)),"% of its land a year
", number(burnt)," hectares a year"), hoverinfo="text", colorbar=list(title=list(text="Land burnt
each year"),tickvals=1:7,ticktext=class_names, len=0.8,thickness=14)) %>% chart(paste0("Land burnt in an average year, % of each country, ",first_year,"–",last_year), paste0("GWIS (MODIS), via Our World in Data; land areas: World Bank. ", "Grey: no land area in the World Bank's data."), geo=list(showframe=FALSE,showcoastlines=FALSE,showland=TRUE,landcolor="#e8e8e8", projection=list(type="natural earth"),lataxis=list(range=c(-57,85))), margin=list(t=50,b=40,l=0,r=0),note_y=-0.02) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: **In Europe, most of it is Ukraine's.** Without Russia, Europe burnt 2.5 million hectares a year, 0.4% of its land, and 66% of that was in Ukraine, which burnt 2.9% of its own land every year, mostly fields (section 3). The countries of Europe's south burn far less of their land: Portugal 1.39% a year, Greece 0.50%, Spain 0.23% and Italy 0.29%. --- ## 2. Is the world burning more than it used to? ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} changes<-do.call(rbind,lapply(split(with_world,with_world$group),function(x) { data.frame(group=x$group[1], start=mean(x$all[x$year%in%first_five]), end=mean(x$all[x$year%in%last_five]), chance=chance(x$all,x$year)) })) rownames(changes)<-NULL changes$change<-100*(changes$end/changes$start-1) of_change<-function(g,column) { result<-changes[[column]][changes$group==g] return(result) } world_fall<-of_change("World","start")-of_change("World","end") africa_part<-100*(of_change("Africa","start")-of_change("Africa","end"))/world_fall north_america<-yearly[yearly$group=="North America",] without_2023<-mean(north_america$all[north_america$year%in%setdiff(last_five,2023)]) falls<-changes[changes$group!="World"&changes$change<=-30,] ``` ::: **Less, by about a fifth.** In 2002–2006 fires burnt 450 million hectares a year, in 2021–2025 353: 22% less. And the fall is not just a matter of a few good years at the end: a rank test of all the years finds it too (the chance of a pattern as strong as this one without a trend is less than 1 in 100). The table compares the first and the last five years, million hectares a year. The last column is the chance, in 100, of a pattern as strong as that of all the years without a trend. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} knitr::kable(data.frame(group=changes$group, start=million(changes$start), end=million(changes$end), change=change_text(changes$change), chance=changes$chance), col.names=c("",paste0(min(first_five),"–",max(first_five)), paste0(min(last_five),"–",max(last_five)),"Change","By chance, in 100"), align="lrrrr") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} | | 2002–2006| 2021–2025| Change| By chance, in 100| |:---------------------|---------:|---------:|------:|-----------------:| |World | 450| 353| −22%| less than 1| |Africa | 299| 238| −20%| less than 1| |Oceania | 52| 43| −18%| 35| |South America | 37| 31| −17%| 20| |Asia | 36| 20| −43%| less than 1| |Russia | 15| 8.7| −43%| less than 1| |North America | 8.7| 11| +28%| 55| |Europe without Russia | 2.8| 1.6| −42%| 4| ::: ::: **Most of the fall is Africa's.** 63% of the land that the world stopped burning was in Africa, which burnt 20% less. Asia, Russia and Europe without Russia burnt 42% to 43% less, but they burn far less land than Africa to begin with. Only North America burnt more, by 28%, and mostly because of 2023: the other four of its last five years burnt 6% more than its first five. This is not new. Satellites found the same from 1998 to 2015: the land burnt in the world fell by about a quarter, most of all in the savannas, and mainly because farming spread and grew more intensive ([Andela et al. 2017](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.aal4108)). ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # the land burnt each year against the group's average of the first five years (= 100), and every # panel on the same scale with_world$index<-100*with_world$all/changes$start[match(with_world$group,changes$group)] index_range<-range(with_world$index)+c(-0.05,0.05)*diff(range(with_world$index)) # one panel: a group's land burnt each year, and the average of its last five years in red trend_panel<-function(g) { x<-with_world[with_world$group==g,] level<-100*changes$end[changes$group==g]/changes$start[changes$group==g] result<-plot_ly(x,x=~year,y=~index,type="scatter",mode="lines+markers", line=list(color=dark_gray,width=1),marker=list(color=dark_gray,size=4), hovertemplate=paste0(g,", %{x}: %{y:.0f}")) %>% add_segments(x=min(last_five)-0.4,xend=max(last_five)+0.4,y=level,yend=level, line=list(color=red,width=3), hovertemplate=paste0(g,", ",min(last_five),"–",max(last_five), ": %{y:.0f}")) %>% layout(xaxis=list(title="",tickvals=c(2005,2015,2025)), yaxis=list(title="",tickvals=seq(50,250,50),range=index_range)) return(result) } panels<-c("World",groups) p<-subplot(lapply(panels,trend_panel),nrows=2,shareX=TRUE,shareY=TRUE,margin=c(0.02,0.02,0.11,0.11)) # above each panel its group and change, and across it a line at 100 domains<-plotly_build(p)$x$layout panel_titles<-list() lines_at_100<-list() for(k in seq_along(panels)) { x_axis<-c("",2:4)[(k-1)%%4+1] y_axis<-c("",2)[(k-1)%/%4+1] change<-changes$change[changes$group==panels[k]] panel_titles[[k]]<-list(text=paste0("",sub("without ","without
",panels[k]),"
", change_text(change)), x=domains[[paste0("xaxis",x_axis)]]$domain[1],xref="paper", y=domains[[paste0("yaxis",y_axis)]]$domain[2],yref="paper",xanchor="left", yanchor="bottom",align="left",showarrow=FALSE,font=list(size=12)) lines_at_100[[k]]<-list(type="line",xref=paste0("x",x_axis," domain"),x0=0,x1=1, yref=paste0("y",y_axis),y0=100,y1=100,layer="below", line=list(color="#bfbfbf",width=1)) } p %>% chart(paste0("Land burnt each year, the average of ",min(first_five),"–",max(first_five), " = 100"), paste0("GWIS (MODIS), via Our World in Data. Red: the average of ",min(last_five),"–", max(last_five),", and the change, under each name."), annotations=panel_titles,shapes=lines_at_100,showlegend=FALSE,margin=list(t=110,b=70), note_y=-0.08) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: --- ## 3. What burns: forest, savanna, grassland or fields? ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} cover_totals<-aggregate(with_world[names(covers)],list(group=with_world$group),sum) cover_shares<-cover_totals cover_shares[names(covers)]<-100*cover_totals[names(covers)]/rowSums(cover_totals[names(covers)]) of_cover<-function(g,k) { result<-cover_shares[[k]][cover_shares$group==g] return(result) } # the world, by kind of land: the first and the last five years, and the trend over all the years world_covers<-do.call(rbind,lapply(names(covers)[1:4],function(k) { data.frame(cover=covers[[k]], start=mean(world[[k]][world$year%in%first_five]), end=mean(world[[k]][world$year%in%last_five]), chance=chance(world[[k]],world$year)) })) world_covers$change<-100*(world_covers$end/world_covers$start-1) of_world_cover<-function(name,column) { result<-world_covers[[column]][world_covers$cover==name] return(result) } # the forest burnt in a group: the first and the last five years, and the trend forest_in<-function(g,column) { x<-yearly[yearly$group==g,] result<-list(start=mean(x$forest[x$year%in%first_five]),end=mean(x$forest[x$year%in%last_five]), chance=chance(x$forest,x$year))[[column]] return(result) } ukraine_crops<-100*in_country("Ukraine","crops")/ sum(countries$crops[countries$group=="Europe without Russia"]) ``` ::: **Mostly savanna, shrubs and grass; forest is a small part.** Of all the land that burnt in the world from 2002 to 2025, 44% was savanna, 40% shrubland and grassland, 8% cropland and 8% forest. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} rows<-factor(cover_shares$group,levels=rev(c("World",groups))) p<-plot_ly() # each kind of land, with a label only on the larger parts for(k in names(covers)) { p<-add_bars(p,x=cover_shares[[k]],y=rows,name=covers[[k]],orientation="h", marker=list(color=cover_colors[[k]],line=list(color="white",width=1.5)), text=ifelse(cover_shares[[k]]>=12,percent(cover_shares[[k]]),""), textposition="inside",insidetextanchor="middle", textfont=list(color=if(k=="forest") "white" else "#1a1a1a"), hovertemplate=paste0("%{y}: %{x:.1f}% ",tolower(covers[[k]]),"")) } p %>% chart(paste0("What burnt, % of the land burnt, ",first_year,"–",last_year), "GWIS (MODIS burned area and land cover), via Our World in Data.", x_axis=list(range=c(0,100),ticksuffix="%",showgrid=FALSE),barmode="stack", legend=c(legend_top,list(traceorder="normal")),uniformtext=list(minsize=10,mode="hide"), margin=list(l=150,t=100,b=70,r=10),note_y=-0.1) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: **What the satellites call savanna.** GWIS lays the burnt land on NASA's map of land cover, made from the same MODIS images ([GWIS country profiles](https://gwis.jrc.ec.europa.eu/apps/country.profile/downloads)), and that map sorts land by how much of it trees cover, not by climate: forest is land where trees cover more than 60% of the ground, savanna land where they cover between 10% and 60% ([MODIS land cover user guide](https://lpdaac.usgs.gov/documents/1409/MCD12_User_Guide_V61.pdf)). In Africa, South America and Australia that is the savanna of the word, grass under scattered trees. In Russia and Canada, where there is no tropical savanna, it takes in northern forest with gaps between the trees, which is why 49% of Russia's burnt land and 49% of North America's counts as savanna. **Europe burns fields.** Without Russia, 76% of the land that burnt in Europe was cropland, 77% of it in Ukraine; forest, as the satellites define it, was 2.7%. **Savanna, grassland and fields burn less; forest, not clearly.** In the world, by kind of land, million hectares a year: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} knitr::kable(data.frame(cover=world_covers$cover, start=million(world_covers$start), end=million(world_covers$end), change=change_text(world_covers$change), chance=world_covers$chance), col.names=c("",paste0(min(first_five),"–",max(first_five)), paste0(min(last_five),"–",max(last_five)),"Change","By chance, in 100"), align="lrrrr") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} | | 2002–2006| 2021–2025| Change| By chance, in 100| |:-----------------------|---------:|---------:|------:|-----------------:| |Forest | 33| 28| −14%| 11| |Savanna | 193| 155| −20%| less than 1| |Shrubland and grassland | 183| 144| −21%| less than 1| |Cropland | 40| 25| −37%| less than 1| ::: ::: The burnt cropland fell the most, 37%, and savanna, shrubland and grassland by about a fifth, all with clear trends. The burnt forest fell by 14%, but a pattern like that would come up by chance 11 times in 100 without a trend. In North America the forest that burnt rose from 1.0 million hectares a year in 2002–2006 to 1.7 in 2021–2025 (by chance less than 1 in 100); in Russia it fell, from 1.1 to 0.5. --- ## 4. When does each continent burn? ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} seasons_of<-weekly[weekly$year<=last_season,] # each group: the share of the year's burnt land in each week, the average of the years season_weeks<-week_parts(by_group(seasons_of[,c("entity","code","week","area_ha")],time="week")) season_weeks<-aggregate(area_ha~group+year+w,data=season_weeks,FUN=sum) season_weeks$share<-100*season_weeks$area_ha/ ave(season_weeks$area_ha,season_weeks$group,season_weeks$year,FUN=sum) season<-aggregate(share~group+w,data=season_weeks,FUN=mean) season$month<-month_of(season$w) by_month<-aggregate(share~month+group,data=season,FUN=sum) # the three months in a row in which each group burns the most (December to February included) three<-function(shares) { result<-sapply(1:12,function(m) sum(shares[(m-1+0:2)%%12+1])) return(result) } in_three<-tapply(by_month$share,by_month$group,three) best<-data.frame(group=names(in_three),start=sapply(in_three,which.max),share=sapply(in_three,max)) months_of<-function(g) { s<-best$start[best$group==g] result<-(s-1+0:2)%%12+1 return(result) } season_text<-function(g) { m<-months_of(g) result<-paste(month.name[m[1]],"to",month.name[m[3]]) return(result) } season_share<-function(g) { result<-percent(best$share[best$group==g]) return(result) } # the countries that burn the most of a group's land in its three months countries_weekly<-seasons_of[seasons_of$code%in%country_codes,] countries_weekly$group<-group_of(countries_weekly$code) leaders<-function(g,n=2) { x<-countries_weekly[countries_weekly$group==g&month_of(countries_weekly$w)%in%months_of(g),] s<-sort(tapply(x$area_ha,x$entity,sum),decreasing=TRUE) result<-and_list(paste0(with_the(names(s)[1:n])," (",percent(100*s[1:n]/sum(s)),")")) return(result) } # the share of a country's burnt land in some months in_months<-function(name,months) { x<-countries_weekly[countries_weekly$entity==name,] result<-percent(100*sum(x$area_ha[month_of(x$w)%in%months])/sum(x$area_ha)) return(result) } ``` ::: **Each in its own dry season, and Africa in two.** The chart shows, for each group, how the land it burns is spread over the year: the share of a year's burnt land in each week, on average from 2012 to 2024. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} season$class<-as.integer(cut(season$share,c(-Inf,0.5,1,2,3,4,Inf))) season_classes<-c("Under 0.5%","0.5–1%","1–2%","2–3%","3–4%","4% or more") middle_of_month<-(as.integer(format(as.Date(paste0("2001-",1:12,"-15")),"%j"))-1)/7+1 plot_ly(season,x=~w,y=~group,z=~class,type="heatmap",zmin=0.5,zmax=6.5, colorscale=color_steps(oranges[2:7]),xgap=1,ygap=1, text=~paste0(group,", ",month.abb[month],", week ",w,": ",two(share), "% of the year's burnt land"), hoverinfo="text", colorbar=list(title=list(text="Share of the year's burnt land in each week",side="top"), orientation="h",x=0,xanchor="left",y=-0.1,yanchor="top",tickvals=1:6, ticktext=season_classes,len=0.9,thickness=12,tickfont=list(size=10))) %>% chart(paste0("When each continent burns, ",first_week_year,"–",last_season), "GWIS (MODIS and VIIRS), via Our World in Data.", x_axis=list(tickvals=middle_of_month,ticktext=month.abb,range=c(0.5,52.5),showgrid=FALSE, zeroline=FALSE), y_axis=list(categoryorder="array",categoryarray=rev(groups),showgrid=FALSE), margin=list(l=150,t=60,b=120,r=10),note_y=-0.36) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: **Africa** burns the most from July to September, 40% of the land it burns in a year, but it has two seasons, one on each side of the equator, each in its own dry months: 88% of South Sudan's burnt land burns from November to February, and 88% of Angola's from June to September. **South America** burns from August to October (61%), most of it in Brazil (71%) and Bolivia (13%), and **Oceania** from September to November (41%), almost all of it in Australia. **Asia** burns from February to April (65%), mostly in Myanmar (27%), India (20%) and Laos (15%). **North America** burns most in spring too, from March to May (49%), mostly in Mexico (44%), the United States (20%) and Honduras (10%); Canada's fires come later, 58% of its burnt land in July and August. **Russia** has a spring season and a summer one: 37% of its burnt land in April and May, 37% in July and August. So has Ukraine, which burns most of the rest of Europe: 26% of its burnt land in March and April, 67% from July to October. --- ## 5. Which were the worst years? ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} co2_groups<-by_group(co2) co2_groups<-co2_groups[co2_groups$year<=last_season,] first_co2<-min(co2_groups$year) worst<-do.call(rbind,lapply(split(co2_groups,co2_groups$group),function(x) { data.frame(group=x$group[1], average=mean(x$co2), worst_year=x$year[which.max(x$co2)], worst=max(x$co2)) })) worst$times<-worst$worst/worst$average worst<-worst[order(-worst$times),] rownames(worst)<-NULL of_worst<-function(g,column) { result<-worst[[column]][worst$group==g] return(result) } co2_in<-function(g,year) { result<-co2_groups$co2[co2_groups$group==g&co2_groups$year==year] return(result) } canada<-cover[cover$entity=="Canada",] oceania<-yearly[yearly$group=="Oceania",] asia<-yearly[yearly$group=="Asia",] in_year<-function(x,year,column="all") { result<-x[[column]][x$year==year] return(result) } ``` ::: **Where fire is rare, the worst years stand out the most.** Burnt land is one measure of a bad year; the carbon dioxide that the fires released is another, which counts the fires that burn forest and peat for more than those of grass. For each group, from 2003 to 2024, million tonnes of carbon dioxide: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} knitr::kable(data.frame(group=worst$group, average=number(worst$average/1e6), year=worst$worst_year, worst=number(worst$worst/1e6), times=one(worst$times)), col.names=c("","A year on average","Worst year","That year","Times the average"), align="lrrrr") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} | | A year on average| Worst year| That year| Times the average| |:---------------------|-----------------:|----------:|---------:|-----------------:| |North America | 560| 2023| 1,548| 2.8| |Russia | 570| 2003| 1,304| 2.3| |Oceania | 495| 2012| 1,009| 2.0| |Asia | 811| 2015| 1,508| 1.9| |Europe without Russia | 33| 2007| 54| 1.6| |South America | 1,053| 2007| 1,679| 1.6| |Africa | 2,907| 2007| 3,365| 1.2| ::: ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} set.seed(2026) strip<-co2_groups strip$of_average<-100*strip$co2/ave(strip$co2,strip$group) strip$is_worst<-strip$co2==ave(strip$co2,strip$group,FUN=max) ranked<-rev(worst$group) # the most extreme worst year at the top strip$position<-match(strip$group,ranked)+runif(nrow(strip),-0.17,0.17) dots<-function(p,x,color) { result<-add_markers(p,data=x,x=~of_average,y=~position, marker=list(color=color,size=9,line=list(color="white",width=1)), text=~paste0(group," ",year,": ",number(co2/1e6)," million tonnes, ", round(of_average),"% of its average"), hovertemplate="%{text}",showlegend=FALSE) return(result) } # the worst year of each group, next to its dot worst_labels<-lapply(seq_along(ranked),function(i) { list(x=100*of_worst(ranked[i],"times"),y=i,text=of_worst(ranked[i],"worst_year"),showarrow=FALSE, xanchor="left",xshift=8,font=list(size=12,color=dark_gray)) }) plot_ly() %>% dots(strip[!strip$is_worst,],gray) %>% dots(strip[strip$is_worst,],red) %>% chart(paste0("CO₂ from fires, % of each group's average, ",first_co2,"–",last_season), "GWIS (MODIS and VIIRS), via Our World in Data. Dots: years; red: the worst year.", x_axis=list(rangemode="tozero",ticksuffix="%"), y_axis=list(tickvals=seq_along(ranked),ticktext=ranked,range=c(0.4,length(ranked)+0.6), zeroline=FALSE), annotations=worst_labels, shapes=list(list(type="line",x0=100,x1=100,yref="paper",y0=0,y1=1, line=list(color=dark_gray,width=1))), margin=list(l=150,t=70,b=90,r=40),note_y=-0.14) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: - **North America, 2023**: 1,548 million tonnes, 2.8 times its average. Canada had the worst fire season in its records, about 15 million hectares by its own count, from mid-April to late October, after an early snowmelt and a drought, in a season 2.2 °C warmer than the average of 1991–2020 ([Jain et al. 2024](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-024-51154-7)). MODIS mapped 13 million hectares in Canada that year, 5 times its average: the satellites miss part of what burns. - **Russia, 2003**: 1,304 million tonnes, 2.3 times its average. - **Asia, 2015**: 1,508 million tonnes, 1.9 times its average, though the land it burnt that year, 33 million hectares, was only 18% above its average. In September and October forests and peat burnt across the islands of South-East Asia, above all in Indonesia, after a long drought, and for those two months the fires released 11.3 million tonnes of carbon dioxide a day, more than the fossil fuels of the EU, 8.9 million tonnes a day ([Huijnen et al. 2016](https://doi.org/10.1038/srep26886)). Peat is soil made of dead plants, full of carbon. - **Oceania, 2012**: its worst year for burnt land too, 90 million hectares, 90% of it shrubland and grassland. The fires that most people remember came later: between September 2019 and early January 2020, about 5.8 million hectares of mainly temperate broadleaf forest burnt in New South Wales and Victoria ([Boer et al. 2020](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41558-020-0716-1)). In MODIS, 3.3 million hectares of forest burnt in Oceania in 2019, 6 times its average, but that is a small part of the 36 million hectares it burnt that year. - **Africa**, which burns the most, is the steadiest: its worst year, 2007, released only 1.2 times its average. And for the rest of Europe the worst year was 2007, the year of Greece's worst fires ([Greece Burning](ILLUSTRATION_GREEK_WILDFIRES.html)). --- ## So, what does it mean? 1. **Most of the world's fire is African.** Africa has 67% of the land that burns; the land it burns in a year is as large as 9% of the continent. Europe without Russia burns 0.4% of its land a year. 2. **The world burns less than it did**: 22% less in 2021–2025 than in 2002–2006, 63% of the fall in Africa. 3. **Forest is a small part of what burns, and it is not clearly burning less.** In North America more of it burns. 4. **Every continent burns in its own dry months**, and Africa has two seasons, one on each side of the equator. 5. **The worst years come where fire is rarer.** North America released 2.8 times its average carbon dioxide in 2023; Africa's worst year, only 1.2 times. **What this does not show.** The satellites map the land that burnt, not what started the fire, and they miss small fires and fires under cloud or trees; the fires here include those that people set on purpose. A continent is large, and its average hides countries that burn far more or far less. The carbon dioxide is an estimate, from GWIS's figures up to 2024. And hectares do not count the people, the homes and the animals lost in the fires, or the smoke that people breathe far from them. For one country close up, see [Greece Burning](ILLUSTRATION_GREEK_WILDFIRES.html); for the heat that dries out the land, [Athens Is Getting Hotter](ILLUSTRATION_ATHENS_HEAT.html); for the temperature of the world, the [NASA GISS Global Temperature Anomaly](ILLUSTRATION_CLIMATE_HIGHCHARTER.html). --- ## Sources - GWIS, the [Global Wildfire Information System](https://gwis.jrc.ec.europa.eu/): the [country profiles](https://gwis.jrc.ec.europa.eu/apps/country.profile/downloads), with the land burnt each year by kind of land since 2002, from MODIS (MCD64A1 burned area, MCD12 land cover); the [seasonal trends](https://gwis.jrc.ec.europa.eu/apps/gwis.statistics/seasonaltrend), with the land burnt each week and the carbon dioxide, from MODIS and VIIRS; [data licence](https://gwis.jrc.ec.europa.eu/about-gwis/data-license), CC BY 4.0. - Our World in Data, [Wildfires](https://ourworldindata.org/wildfires): the GWIS figures by country and continent, from its charts [annual-burned-area-by-landcover](https://ourworldindata.org/grapher/annual-burned-area-by-landcover), [weekly-area-burnt-by-wildfires](https://ourworldindata.org/grapher/weekly-area-burnt-by-wildfires) and [annual-carbon-dioxide-emissions](https://ourworldindata.org/grapher/annual-carbon-dioxide-emissions); the [land area](https://ourworldindata.org/grapher/land-area-km) of each country, from the World Bank; its [continents](https://ourworldindata.org/grapher/continents-according-to-our-world-in-data) (CC BY 4.0). - Giglio, L. et al.
